transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I had to come in because I'm being watched constantly, and I don't know who to trust anymore. There are people monitoring my apartment and tracking my movements wherever I go. I just need some help dealing with this.
Have you been feeling unusually down or depressed, or alternatively, unusually energized, elevated, or irritable lately?
No, I haven't been feeling unusually depressed or energized lately. Aside from the stress of being watched, my mood has been pretty normal.
How long have you been feeling like you're being watched and monitored?
It's been going on for about a year and ten months now, almost two years. It started back then and hasn't stopped for a single day, and I'm just constantly on edge.
Despite these experiences, have you been able to manage your daily responsibilities, like work, school, or taking care of yourself?

Yes, I'm still able to go to work and take care of my daily responsibilities without any major issues. Aside from the stress and distraction of constantly being watched, my day-to-day functioning is pretty normal.
Have you ever heard voices, seen things, or had other sensory experiences that others don't seem to notice?
No, I've never heard any strange voices or seen things that aren't actually there. My senses are completely normal, and I only see the real people who are actively watching and tracking me.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Delusional Disorder"], and the current candidates remain the same. The patient reports a persistent, non-bizarre delusion (being monitored and watched) for nearly two years, without impairment in daily functioning, mood episodes, or hallucinations. The absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thinking, or mood symptoms makes schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, and mood disorders with psychotic features unlikely. The fixed false belief with preserved functioning strongly supports Delusional Disorder.
